subject: Post-call: migration readiness + OpenAI-compat sanity tests
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@finlytics.com>, Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: migration readiness + OpenAI-compat sanity tests

Thanks again for the time this morning — good conversation and clear priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Goal: validate that Finlytics can migrate a subset of bursty inference traffic (analytics summarization + entity extraction) off your current hyperscaler endpoints with parity on latency and no regression on outputs.

2) Must-haves for pilot:
- OpenAI-compatible API (exact request/response shape) for minimal SDK changes
- Function-calling parity for extraction flows
- Throughput checks at your 95th percentile burst (approx 60 rps sustained for 3-minute windows)
- Prompt-diff comparisons and a small QoR (quality) eval suite (~50 golden examples)

3) Proposed next tests (we can run these in a 5-business-day run):
- Sanity: 50 prompt diffs vs Bedrock and current OpenAI baseline
- Load: 60 rps sustained, 1 minute and 3 minute windows
- Latency SLO: p95 target within 1.2x of current baseline for 512-token avg
- Function-calling: confirm 1:1 mapping for your extraction schema

I attached a short checklist that maps those tests to responsibilities and artifacts (redwood-openai-compat-checklist.pdf). Can you confirm the sandbox credentials you want us to use (infra@finlytics?) and any blackout windows for the next two weeks? Once you confirm, Rafael (cc'd) will propose a concrete test matrix and sample curl/SDK swaps.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-openai-compat-checklist.pdf (2 pages)]

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@finlytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@finlytics.com>
Cc: infra@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-08-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: migration readiness + OpenAI-compat sanity tests

Thanks Vanessa — that looks good. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock the window: 

- For the "OpenAI-compatible API" ask: we need function-calling parity (names + param schema) and identical streaming behavior for our frontend. Any differences in chunking or event types will require minor client changes.
- For throughput: our 95th-percentile bursts sometimes spike to ~90 rps for 90s; can the test include a 90 rps short burst as an optional stress run?
- Please include a simple SDK swap path for Python and Node — we have a couple of helper libs that wrap openai.ChatCompletion/Responses.

Also, can you expose a sandbox API key with rate limits set to the test windows? infra@finlytics will own creds. If we like the results we'll move to a small pilot (1-2 dedicated nodes) and then prod rollout.

Ethan
Senior Engineering Manager, Finlytics
[Sent from my iPhone]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@finlytics.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: migration readiness + OpenAI-compat sanity tests — test plan + runbook

Ethan — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a pragmatic test matrix and concrete artifacts we'll provide. Plan assumes Redwood-hosted sandbox endpoints and a short ramp for the stress run. Timeline: 3 business days to set up + 2 business days to run/collect results.

Test matrix (high level):
- Sanity (functional): 50 golden prompts, compare tokens + top-3 completions + function result payloads. Pass if extraction schema fields match and edit-distance on key fields < 8%.
- Load (main): 60 rps sustained for 3 minutes. Optional stress: 90 rps for 90s. We'll produce per-second traces and p95/p99 latency windows.
- Streaming/Chunk parity: send same streaming payloads, assert event order and chunk boundaries; if difference is detected we'll provide a shim for the front-end to reassemble.
- SDK swap: provide two artifacts — a) python-sample-swap.py that maps openai.ChatCompletion -> redwood.responses; b) node-swap.js for Response streaming. Both will be small drop-in examples you can run in <10 lines in most callsites.

Sample curl (OpenAI-compatible):
curl -X POST "https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/responses" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-open-3b", "input":"Summarize: ...", "max_tokens":256}'

Sample Python swap (snippet):
# original: from openai import OpenAI
# new: import requests
import requests
resp = requests.post('https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/responses', headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY'}, json={"model":"rw-open-3b","input":"Summarize: ..."})
print(resp.json())

Notes on models & quantization: we'll default to rw-open-3b-q4 for latency parity; if you prefer higher quality we'll run rw-open-7b-ptq as a second pass. For SDKs that use streaming, our endpoint mirrors the OpenAI response stream using the same event prefixes; small differences in chunking can be handled client-side.

Artifacts we'll share:
- redwood-test-scripts.zip (load scripts + prompt diffs)
- raw traces + per-route dashboards (shared link)
- high-level report with pass/fail and recommended next steps

If this plan looks good Vanessa, we'll request sandbox creds for infra@finlytics and schedule the setup call — ideally tomorrow afternoon.

— Rafael
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-test-scripts.zip]
